subject: Urgent: quota handoff causing sustained throttling for Satori Health
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena@satorihealth.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Satori Health - Platform Team <ops@satorihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Degraded throughput and 429s since Friday — urgent

Sergio —

We're seeing sustained 429s and high tail latency from Friday afternoon through our peak windows. Error rate climbed to ~8% and effective throughput dropped by ~35% compared to baseline. This is significantly impacting our nightly ingestion jobs.

We shared a sample of request logs and our expected token profiles (attached). Can you confirm whether any quota/burst policy change rolled out to our account or on the platform? Our workspace was recently moved from the shared pool to a reserved capacity lane last month; this started after that change.

We need a temporary mitigation (higher burst allowance or routing fallback) until root cause is identified. Please escalate — this is now blocking production ops.

Thanks,
Elena Cruz
Director, Platform Engineering
Satori Health

To: Elena Cruz <elena@satorihealth.com>

Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Degraded throughput and 429s since Friday — urgent

Elena —

Thanks for the log dump; seeing it now. I'm looping in Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik from Product Ops to triage. Initial ask: can you confirm the exact timestamps of the ingestion jobs and whether requests are coming from multiple regions? That helps rule out routing/regional capacity.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Karthik will validate the quota and burst windows for the Satori tenant (we suspect a misaligned handoff between shared and reserved configs).
- I will request a temporary burst override if we detect suppressed burst tokens.
- Marissa will coordinate comms and any potential credit/ SLA remediation if this is our config issue.

We aim to have an initial update within 4 hours.

Sergio
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Elena Cruz <elena@satorihealth.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2029 12:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Degraded throughput and 429s since Friday — urgent

Team / Elena —

Preliminary findings after a quick audit: when Satori's workspace was moved to Dedicated last month, an automated migration applied a conservative burst-window profile that caps burst tokens per minute lower than their previous shared-pool allowance. Additionally, an orphaned quota window configuration left a short, tight per-second burst bucket active for some request patterns. Combined, this causes sustained suppression when they run concurrent ingestion threads.

What I observed:
- Config A (legacy shared): burst window = 120s, burst tokens = 900
- Config B (post-migration): burst window = 60s, burst tokens = 240
- Orphaned per-second bucket: 12 tokens/sec for a short safety window

Impact: for multi-threaded ingestion we throttle aggressively and push many requests into retry, spiking tail latency and 429s.

Immediate mitigation I propose:
1) Apply a temporary burst override to match legacy burst_tokens for the weekend windows.
2) Remove/merge orphaned per-second window.
3) Create a short-lived routing fallback to a compatible model variant if capacity saturates.

I'll implement 1 & 2 in the staging control plane now and roll to prod after smoke checks. ETA for change rollout: ~2 hours.

Karthik
Product Operations
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, Elena Cruz <elena@satorihealth.com>, amir.patel <amir@consulting-partners.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jul 2029 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Degraded throughput and 429s since Friday — urgent

Quick status update and exec flag:

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick triage. Karthik completed the staging rollout overnight and ran the smoke tests this morning. Results:
- Burst tokens now aligned with legacy profile for Satori during their 22:00-03:00 ET window.
- Removed the orphaned per-second bucket.
- We saw error rate drop from 8% -> 0.7% in the test window and throughput recover ~28%.

However, given the customer impact and that the misconfiguration originated from an automated migration script, I'm routing an executive note to Product + Reliability leadership for a postmortem and an exception review on tooling that creates handoff configs. Grace — can you please take this as a follow-on? We should consider:
- A migration checklist and a preflight validation that compares legacy and target burst profiles.
- Alerting on sudden burst token delta on migration runs.
- Short-term credit or SLA concession discussion with Satori (Marissa to lead).

Elena — apologies for the impact. We'll keep monitoring and follow up with a formal postmortem and remediation plan by Friday.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
[attachment: satori_sla_report.pdf]
From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena@satorihealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jul 2029 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Degraded throughput and 429s since Friday — urgent

Following up with the exec asks and next steps:

1) Postmortem scope: migration automation that transforms quota/burst profiles + lack of delta alerting. Deliverable: RCA and action items — due 2029-07-25.
2) Short-term controls: add pre-migration validation (compare aggregate token allotment and per-window limits) and a one-click rollback safety switch for the migrator.
3) Customer remediation: Marissa, propose a one-month credit and an SLA credit if error rate exceeded 2% in any 24h window during the incident; draft sent to Elena for approval.

Operational notes:
- Karthik's changes are live and we're monitoring telemetry. Early signals are steady.
- I'm assigning an engineer to own migration-tooling hardening and another to implement the delta alerting (internal ticket: MIG-4533).

Elena — we'll keep you updated hourly until baseline is stable for 72 hours. Appreciate your patience and the logs; they helped pinpoint the handoff gap quickly.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
